note: AVG over loans reached through disp. In this data no loan is joined to more than one male client, so no row repeats; the deduplicated rewrite returns the same value. The SQL alone cannot show this.
rewrite_sql: SELECT AVG(amount) FROM loan WHERE account_id IN (SELECT d.account_id FROM disp d JOIN client c ON c.client_id = d.client_id WHERE c.gender = 'M')

note: AVG over card withdrawals reached through card and disp. No 1998 withdrawal row repeats in this data; the deduplicated rewrite returns the same value. The SQL alone cannot show this.
rewrite_sql: SELECT AVG(amount) FROM trans WHERE account_id IN (SELECT d.account_id FROM card k JOIN disp d ON d.disp_id = k.disp_id) AND STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '1998' AND operation = 'VYBER KARTOU'

note: The query filters to one client, and every client has exactly one disp row, so each trans row is joined once. The guard cannot see this data-level uniqueness from the SQL.
rewrite_sql: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM trans WHERE account_id IN (SELECT account_id FROM disp WHERE client_id = 617) AND STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '1998'
